text:
customer_jtaylor: Hey team — starting ~08:10 UTC our EU customers (FR/DE) see 401s and huge latency. Ticket opened with billing spike. Appears requests are landing in us-west. Anyone else seeing cross-region routing?

beth_support_lead: Sorry for the trouble, JT. Can you share a request-id and a curl example? Any `x-pop`/`x-region` headers?

customer_jtaylor: request-id: rq_9f3b7c. Sample curl attached: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_****\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat` Response headers include `x-pop: us-west-1`, `x-auth-status: 401`. Token is for eu-dedicated tenant.

elaine_support: pinging @sam_netops @mike_infra — this smells like GeoIP/EDNS handoff. Could be stale geoip db or an upstream resolver returning US network blocks.

sam_netops: I see an anomaly. From our edge logs the source IPs for those flows are FR client IPs but the geoip lookup resolved to US region for the ASNs. Checking recent GeoIP DB update history. Give me the dig output from an affected client (preferably from their ISP) so we can inspect EDNS behaviour.

customer_jtaylor: here you go (from house broadband in Paris):

```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai
34.209.123.45

$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
34.209.123.45

$ dig +short api.redwood.ai +short
34.209.123.45
```

Also traceroute shows hop to us-west region before hitting our edge.

mike_infra: Can you curl with `-I` and include `Accept-Language`? Need full response headers. Also confirm if requests have `edns-client-subnet` from their resolver.

customer_jtaylor: I captured headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Server: redwood-edge
x-pop: us-west-1
x-region: us-west
x-request-id: rq_9f3b7c
x-auth-status: 401
Content-Type: application/json

{\"error\":\"invalid token for tenant eu-123\"}
```

No edns-client-subnet in dig output (using default ISP resolver) — I can ask customer to run `dig +short @resolver api.redwood.ai +edns`.

beth_support_lead: This is causing billing because retries and fallback to fallback-tier route go to higher-cost pool; we saw a spike in token validations and costs. Escalating to infra.

sam_netops: Quick checks from our side: the GeoIP DB auto-sync ran 3h ago, but S3 sync had a transient 503 during the job window, so one edge cluster may still have old mappings. I'm seeing inconsistent country codes across POPs for the same client IP. That would explain cross-region landing.

mike_infra: Agree. Two things: (1) we should purge geoip cache on affected POPs (manual invalidate), (2) temporarily tighten fallback policy to prefer regional variant for auth calls (so tokens don't hit us-west). I can run the purge, but need approval for an emergency config push.

beth_support_lead: Approve emergency purge and policy tweak, monitor for regressions. Notify customers when fixed.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by mike_infra: geoip-cache-invalidate -> targeting pop-eu-1, pop-eu-2. ETA ~5m.

sam_netops: After purge, verify with `curl -I` and also `dig +trace` from client side. Also check resolver logs: some ISPs were returning ETR (carrier NAT) IPs that map to US in our db. We may need to add a short-term exception mapping for those ASN ranges.

customer_jtaylor: running quick check now...

(customer_jtaylor posts 3m later)

customer_jtaylor: Good news — after your purge I see `x-pop: eu-central-1` and 200 responses. Latency back to normal. Thanks.

mike_infra: Confirming metrics: auth 401s back to baseline in eu, billing spike subsiding. Leaving exception mapping as opt-in for now. I opened infra ticket INF-4872 to add more robust handling for stale geoip during sync failures.

elaine_support: Can we document repro steps and mitigations for on-call? Putting short playbook in support-runbook: 
- ask customer to `curl -I` and paste `x-pop/x-region`
- request `dig +short` from at least two public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1)
- if mismatch, ask for traceroute and ISP ASN
- escalate to netops to check geoip sync and S3 job logs
- temporary actions: geoip cache invalidate, regional fallback tighten, ASN exception mapping

beth_support_lead: I'll inform billing ops to reconcile the spike with the account and offer credit if needed. Please attach INF-4872 to the customer ticket.

sam_netops: Post-mortem notes aside: we should add a health check for GeoIP sync consistency across POPs. I'll propose a telemetry alert.

customer_jtaylor: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Would be great if there was a header that indicates whether GeoIP was authoritative or fallback.

mike_infra: Good idea — filing a FR for `x-geo-source` header to indicate authoritative vs fallback. Putting owner on INF-4873.

beth_support_lead: Closing loop: customer notified, issue resolved for their tenant. Leaving thread open until INF-4872/4873 have owners and timelines.

sam_netops: Owner assigned INF-4872 -> sam_netops (ETA 3 days), INF-4873 -> eng-runtime (pending triage).

elaine_support: Adding runbook snippet to internal support doc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy success: geoip-cache-invalidate completed on pop-eu-1,pop-eu-2 at 2250001267.
